newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street expected to weaken at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street expected to weaken at open.

text.p: Wall Street is expected to weaken at the open on Monday, feeling continued profit-taking in the technology sector while training a wary eye on several key corporate earnings results.
Technology stocks, which slumped early on Friday, would likely see more pressure after failing to recoup losses later in the session, analysts said.
The sector would also watch for second quarter earnings results from giant technology company International Business Machines Corp, due Monday after the market close.

"We should open lower because the market failed to have a recovery on Friday," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said. "The major focus will be on earnings and on Greenspan tomorrow. It will also be crucial to see IBM's earnings this afternoon."

While the stock market digested quarterly results from Dow components, including AT&T Corp and Boeing Co, there would be some caution ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual testimony to the House Banking Subcommittee tomorrow, analysts said.

"There will be some caution ahead of Greenspan's speech on Tuesday, and we are likely to see a continued reaction to Friday's declines," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said. "Profit-taking is in evidence."
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was down 2.50 points at 914.40, while the benchmark 30-year Treasury was down 3/32 at a 6.54 percent yield.
On Friday, U.S. stocks succumbed to profit-taking, with the Dow Jones Industrial average sliding around 130 points to close at 7890.

Among closely-watched quarterly results, AT&T Corp posted second quarter earnings of $0.59 per share, compared to $0.92 per share in the year-ago quarter and a First Call consensus estimate of $0.58 per share.
"AT&T has its hands full with its own focus and leadership," Ackerman said. "It has fallen behind the other major telecommunications companies in terms of its focus, formula and leadership."
IBM, which bucked Friday's declines in the tech sector to close higher, eased slightly in London trading ahead of its second quarter results.
It was expected to earn $1.42 per share in the second quarter versus $1.26 per share in last year's second quarter, according to a First Call survey of analysts.
The dollar was trading in a range against the yen in Asia, at around 115.55/60 yen. In Europe, it was robust, trading at 1.7945/50 marks.
Japan's Nikkei average was closed for a holiday.
In London, the FTSE 100 was off 68.2 at 4809.0.
U.S. stocks weakened in London trading, dragged down by further profit-taking in the technology sector.

The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that the future of Apple Computer Inc is viewed differently by short-sellers, who are betting against the computer maker, and by takeover speculators.
